scope: Bounded demand producer, strategic web recipient and tactical/server identity trace. Other producers, authorization policies and independent lenses remain incomplete.
inspection_provenance: Selected ranges were personally inspected in the c100 source checkout; preserved 95e and c100 tree inventories bind identical current blobs. The separate physical-p16 body read retains its original attribution.

candidate.classification: source-derived strategic action failure caused by comparing gateway sender to tactical-assignment identity; supported pending-demand reachability and runtime unverified
candidate.detail: The strategic web form displays observe/refuse for a pending demand, and its selected-character route invokes resolve_religious_demand through the same authenticated database client that registered the nonzero strategic gateway. The reducer instead compares ctx.sender to Character.server. Character construction initializes server to Identity::ZERO; tactical enrollment sets it to the tactical server identity and mission leave clears it. Given a pending demand for an unassigned character, the registered nonzero gateway cannot equal that zero field, so the reducer source returns the player-only error before either choice is applied. The web handler logs an error and redirects. This is a source-derived conditional result; no database, web or runtime probe was performed.
candidate.safeguards: The web page queries a pending demand for the selected character, and the route checks the session character against its character_id path. The reducer checks a living target, pending status, supported choice, and settlement/day constraints for observing a holy day. Registration requires a nonzero authenticated gateway identity. None of those facts establishes production demand creation or a demonstrated player failure.
candidate.connected_scope: Condition refresh and demand creation/expiry; Character.server construction, enrollment and teardown; strategic gateway registration and client identity; session-selected character, route path and demand ownership; observing/refusing effects, authorization helper, simulation ownership and user-facing error handling. The web handler sends only demand_id and choice to the reducer and does not compare the demand row’s character_id with the selected session character in its body; evaluate that relationship before changing the reducer gate.
candidate.proposed_repair: After exhaustive discovery, use the appropriate strategic character-mutation authority rather than tactical assignment, and enforce the intended selected-character-to-demand relationship at the trusted browser boundary or an equivalent authoritative seam. Preserve pending-state, choice and holy-day checks, tactical isolation and intentional simulation access; do not add compatibility paths.
candidate.later_acceptance: After product validation is authorized, exercise observe and refuse for a valid pending demand on an unassigned character through the authorized gateway; ensure the selected character cannot resolve another character’s demand, unauthorized direct senders fail, and intended disposable simulation ownership works if allowed. Check expiry, same-day and settlement rules, failure reporting, and no unintended tactical state persistence.
candidate.relationship_qualification: Both concern strategic character mutation authority but affect distinct reducer and browser boundaries; they are not established duplicates. No exact historical alias is established; historical queue remains unreconciled.
candidate.discovery: partial; demand reachability, owner binding, all entry points, policy and historical aliases remain open

remaining: Trace all demand producers, browser and direct clients, ownership mapping, tactical overlap, simulation policy and historical aliases; independently assess behavior, authority and aggregate-state lenses. No product validation or repair.
